vulnerabilities.description: Session files created with world-writable permissions (0664). Any user on system can read/modify sensitive session context. Found 50+ session files with rw-rw-r-- permissions.
Memory and state files stored without encryption in plain text JSON with world-readable permissions. Files include auto-memory-store.json, graph-state.json, intelligence-snapshot.json.
Key validation regex /^[a-z0-9_]+$/i lacks length constraints. No maximum key length enforced, allowing potential DoS through memory exhaustion.
Temporary files created in system /tmp directory. While random naming prevents collisions, files are world-readable if cleanup fails. No retry mechanism on delete failure.
Session context stored in plain JSON without encryption. Future enhancements could inadvertently store sensitive data like API keys or tokens.
Dependencies use caret ranges (^) allowing automatic patch/minor updates. While generally safe, consider exact pinning for critical dependencies. Run 'npm audit' regularly.
POSITIVE: Public environment variables (GA_MEASUREMENT_ID, ADSENSE_CLIENT) properly prefixed with NEXT_PUBLIC_. No secrets exposed in client code. Compliant with Next.js best practices.

recommendations: 1. Update session.js line 25 and memory.js to use restrictive file permissions: fs.writeFileSync(path, data, { mode: 0o600 })
2. Implement encryption for sensitive stored data using Node.js crypto module
3. Add maximum length validation to memory key: /^[a-z0-9_]{1,64}$/i
4. Add retry logic with exponential backoff for temporary file cleanup
5. Run 'npm audit' and fix any critical vulnerabilities
6. Add SECURITY_POLICY.md documenting secure development practices
7. Implement automated security scanning in CI/CD pipeline
8. Never commit .env files or secrets - maintain .gitignore properly

main_concerns: File permissions misconfiguration on session/memory files
Lack of encryption for stored state data
positive_findings: No hardcoded secrets in source code
No SQL injection risks (no database operations)
No dangerous dangerouslySetInnerHTML usage with user input
